problem:
The number of particles $N(t)$ in a radioactive substance after $t$ years can be modeled by the differential equation

$$
\frac{\text{d}N}{\text{d}t}=-3N.
$$

If there were $8\,500$ particles initially, calculate the number of particles remaining after $2$ years. Round your answer to the nearest integer.

feedback.problem:
The outstanding amount $L(t)$ that Daphne needs to repay the bank $t$ years after taking out a loan can be modeled by the differential equation

$$
\frac{\text{d}L}{\text{d}t}=-0.5L.
$$

If she borrowed $$32\,000,$ calculate the debt remaining after $8$ years. Round your answer to the nearest dollar.
feedback.worked_solution:
We model the amount of debt remaining using the differential equation

$$
\frac{\text{d}L}{\text{d}t}=-0.5L.
$$

The solution to this equation is

$$
L(t)={L}_{0}\,{e}^{-0.5t},
$$

where ${L}_{0}$ is the initial value.

We're told that $$32\,000$ were borrowed, so we have ${L}_{0}=32\,000.$

Therefore, the amount of debt $L$ remaining at time $t$ is

$$
L(t)=32\,000\,{e}^{-0.5t}\,.
$$

Finally, to find the amount of debt remaining when $t=8,$ we substitute $t=8$ into the above, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}L(8) & =32\,000\,{e}^{-0.5\cdot 8} \\  & =32\,000\,{e}^{-4} \\  & ≈586.100\end{aligned}
$$

Rounding our answer to the nearest integer, we conclude that $586$ dollars of debt remain.
